name: 3D Diorama
visualIdentity: A complete miniature stage with deliberate boundaries and consistent scales for architecture, characters, and props. The view is elevated or oblique with limited depth of field. Local actions and environmental detail must not blur key models or paths. The label was normalized from source references, which explicitly name a 3D diorama.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to 3D dioramas, miniature sets, isometric scenes with constrained movement, and layered or 2.5D artwork. Inferred suitability includes campus maps, product ecosystems, and process tours staged as miniatures. Hybrid use with characters or annotations is possible but optional.
limitations: Camera tilt must not break required isometric projection. Movement must not expose incomplete layers or break ground contact. Depth separation must not hide essential labels or moving models. Oversized characters that break miniature scale should be avoided. Soft shadows alone do not establish photorealism. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production.
palette: Reference-dependent example, used only when no approved palette is supplied: background #EEE6D4, foreground #35433C, accent_1 #7B9173, accent_2 #B3885F. Task or reference colors override it. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background contrast is 8.371:1. Accents are decorative only, at 3.04 and 3.27 against foreground.
motionAndInteraction: Motion is driven by composition time, with local actions staged on a bounded stage. Optional motion references are screened for compatibility: parallax (motion-009), camera orbit around a subject (motion-010), chapter transitions (motion-012), story steps (motion-015), exploded reveal (motion-017), dolly (motion-019), and camera orbit (motion-021). Pointer and scroll input apply only to interactive delivery. Sharp cuts remain allowed where deliberate.
audio: Audio is unspecified as a fixed requirement. The source suggests task-specific direction: background music, voiceover, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen from topic, audience, and motion. Explicit user audio choices take priority. No fixed genre, tempo, voice, or mandatory layer is assigned. Speech must stay intelligible, balanced, and free of clipping.
assetRequirements: User-supplied assets are unspecified. Only authorized assets may be used, and an exporter string does not establish authorship. glTF parts need inspected node names, materials, pivots, and embedded animation; clip existence must not be assumed from filenames. Normal and roughness maps are non-color data. Optional hop motion needs creature assets. Motion-010 needs complete geometry or sufficient turntable views.
combinations: Explicit suggestions include style-078 (matte clay-like figures) for characters, sharing one light rig and fixed scale ratios. Style-024 (handwritten callouts) can serve as an annotation layer, with the pointer shown first, then the note, and no annotations during camera moves. Use this style alone when the miniature set itself is the subject. Avoid mixing glossy and matte finishes or adding new accent hues.
productionApproach: Blender with bundled Python bpy and Cycles or EEVEE is the suggested style renderer and motion engine for models, materials, lighting, and offline renders. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for assembly, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Verify decoded opening, key, transition, and closing frames, plus audio sync.
